page: Google Cloud Platform m1-ultramem-160 is a dedicated memory-optimized server type configured for enterprise workloads requiring extensive memory capacity. The instance operates on the x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon processors clocked at 2.2 GHz. It is configured with 80 physical cores and 160 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Cache allocation consists of 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and a 55 MB shared L3 cache. Memory provisioning totals 3844.0 GB, which equals approximately 24.02 GB of RAM per vCPU. The platform contains no integrated local storage and no discrete GPUs, necessitating external storage volumes for disk operations.

Benchmark results highlight significant differences between single-threaded and parallel processing metrics. Single-thread performance is modest, with a Geekbench single-core score of 845.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 846.78, placing both in the lower tenth percentile. Compression throughput is similarly restrained, measuring 18.93 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip. Conversely, aggregate multi-core and memory capabilities are substantial. The instance achieved 80467.0 in multi-core stress-ng tests and a PassMark CPU score of 59126.32. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth reached 245.86 GB/sec, while uncached write bandwidth measured 115.9 GB/sec. Additionally, the instance completed 79.34 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved 48.44 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Hardware tradeoffs focus on raw memory capacity and aggregate parallelism over single-core speed. Workloads that depend on high single-threaded IPC or vector extensions like AVX-512 will experience bottlenecks, as demonstrated by slower text processing and compression metrics. Cost efficiency is qualitatively favorable for organizations that need to consolidate massive memory structures into a single operating system image, avoiding the operational complexity of distributed caching architectures. The hardware profile is suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise in-memory analytics, Redis clusters, and memory-heavy transactional backends.
description: Google Cloud Platform m1-ultramem-160 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 160 vCPUs across 80 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 2.2 GHz x86_64 architecture. The system delivers 3844.0 GB of memory, yielding 24.02 GB per vCPU, with no local storage or GPU accelerators included. Performance benchmarks demonstrate a distinct split: single-threaded scores, including a Geekbench single-core rating of 845.0, sit in the bottom tenth percentile, while aggregate throughput is strong, marked by a multi-core stress-ng score of 80467.0 and uncached memory read bandwidth of 245.86 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput measures 79.34 million operations per second. While not optimal for high single-thread clock requirements, the platform provides resource density for workloads demanding contiguous system memory. It is best suited for enterprise in-memory databases, large caching layers, and high-footprint data processing tasks.
